chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever backbites a believing combatant, or harms him, or stays behind him in his family with evil, a scale will be set up for him on the Day of Resurrection, so his good deeds will be exhausted, then he will be cast into the Fire, if the combatant was in the obedience of Allah, Exalted and Mighty.'

key_terms.خَلَفَهُ فِي أَهْلِهِ: stayed behind in his family / remained with his family

ai.seo_question: What happens to the good deeds of someone who backbites a soldier in battle?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the severe spiritual penalty for undermining a *ghazi* (combatant) in jihad, specifically through backbiting or causing distress to his family. It illustrates the mechanism of *hasanat* (good deeds) being transferred to the combatant as compensation, with Hellfire serving as the fallback if the backbiter's merits are insufficient, provided the combatant remained obedient to God. This underscores the communal importance of supporting those engaged in religious struggle, a key theme in Shia jurisprudence regarding the merits of jihad.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who backbites a Believer combatant, or harms him, or behind him in his family with evil, (Scale) would be set up for him on the Day of Judgement, so his Rewards would be drowned, then he would be responded to be in the Fire, when the combatant was in the obedience of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic’.
en.sarwar: 10. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy from abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, who has said the following:

“If one back-bites a believing person who is fighting for the cause of Allah or troubles the fighter’s family in his absence by evil manners, he will, on the Day of Judgment, be brought to justice. All of his good deeds will become invalid and he will then be sent into hell, if the fighter has fought in obedience to Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious.’”
